title: Batteries State of Health Estimation via Efficient Neural Networks With Multiple Channel Charging Profiles
inputs: charging-profile V, I, T of each cycle subsampled; mean of 10 samples per channel -> 30-dim vector; min-max scaled
evidence: P2c: 'the data at every charging cycle are measured' (III.A); features from whole CC-CV charge profiles (NASA charge starts after full discharge) | baseline: SVR and AdaBoost compared (Tables 4-7)
notes: Full charge profile V/I/T resampled to 10 averaged points per channel; time-to-4.2V is implicit in the resampled shape rather than an explicit feature - P2c judged yes but weaker than an explicit CC-time feature. Min-max normalization over 'charging cycle collection' scope unclear. Reports both 85/15 within-cell and leave-one-battery-out; coded cell_held_out.

title: Li-Ion Batteries Parameter Estimation With Tiny Neural Networks Embedded on Intelligent IoT Microcontrollers
datasets: NASA PCoE (multiple sets; B05,B27,B30,B46 held out)
inputs: 20 time steps of discharge-cycle samples: current, voltage, time difference between samples, temperature
evidence: baseline: 'a Random Forest (RF) model and an SVR model ... used as a baseline' (III.B)
notes: Inputs are 'only some samples for each discharge cycle'; selection rule over the discharge not specified. If the 20 samples span the full discharge, sum of time-difference feature equals discharge time (=Q/I under CC) -> P2 coded unclear. Linear-kernel SVR + RF baselines. Test = one held-out battery per set.

title: Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Monitoring Based on Ensemble Learning
inputs: 6 HFs: IC peak position/height/area, equal-voltage-drop time (discharge window), CC-mode ratio Tcc/(Tcc+Tcv) of charge, sample entropy of discharge voltage
evidence: P2c: 'Tcc represents for the CC charging time ... ratio of CC mode' (IV.1); split: 'cycles 1:2:end as the training sets ... 2:2:end as the testing sets' (V) | P2: 'F6 is the sample entropy of discharging voltage' (IV.A)
notes: CC-charge ratio from NASA CC-CV charge that starts after full discharge -> P2c yes. P2 strength WEAK: sample entropy of the per-cycle discharge voltage series (whole discharge implied, window not explicitly stated); not a time/charge feature. IC curve source (charge vs discharge) not stated. Comparators NN, GPR, KRR, SVM - no linear/tree/mean baseline. Interleaved odd/even cycle split within each cell.

title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Battery Using Empirical Degradation and Error Compensation Models
inputs: empirical degradation model (cycle-based) + BP-NN error compensation with per-cycle average charge current/voltage and average discharge current/voltage
evidence: P2/P2c: 'During each cycle, the average values of charging-discharging current and voltage are calculated' (V.A)
notes: P2 and P2c strength WEAK: statistics (means) over the entire discharge / entire CC-CV charge, not time or charge; mean charge current over CC-CV = Q_ch/t_ch so weakly capacity-linked. Split: 'cross-validation approach ... based on battery B5, B6 and B18' (Table 5 not extractable) -> coded cell_held_out. Comparators: empirical degradation model, LSTM, CNN; no linear/tree/mean ML baseline (empirical cycle model is arguably a simple baseline).

title: A New Hybrid Neural Network Method for State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery
datasets: NASA (B05,06,18,25,27,29,30,31,34 train; B07,28,32,36 test); Oxford Degradation 1
inputs: discharge-curve samples (voltage distribution and capacity changes) converted to 4000x1 vectors, min-max scaled, into dilated CNN-BiGRU
evidence: P2: 'uses the voltage distribution and capacity changes in the extracted battery discharge curve' (Abstract); 'convert the discharge data samples into a vector of size 4000 x 1' (2.4)
notes: P2 STRONG: whole discharge curve incl. capacity changes as input, the curve endpoint is the label capacity. Min-max per data sample (Eq. 12) - not whole-life, P3 no. Test cells disjoint from training cells in both datasets. Comparators: CNN- and RNN-series only.

title: Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation Based on CNN-LSTM-Attention-FVIM Algorithm and Fusion of Multiple Health Features
inputs: 5 charge HFs: equal-voltage-rise charging time, CC charging time, CV charging time, time of charge temperature peak, CC charging time ratio; CNN-LSTM-Attention-FVIM
evidence: P2c: 'constant current charging time, constant voltage charging time ... and constant current charging time ratio' (2.2); split: '70% of the battery data as the training set ... remaining 30% as the …' (5.2)
notes: P2c STRONG: CC charging time from a fully discharged state (NASA CC-CV after full CC discharge; CALCE CS2 same). HFs 'normalized' - scope not stated (P3 unclear). Within-cell chronological 50/60/70% training splits. Comparators GRU, BiLSTM, CNN, CNN-LSTM-Attention only.

title: A Method for Interval Prediction of Satellite Battery State of Health Based on Sample Entropy
inputs: discharge cutoff (end) voltage and sample entropy of discharge voltage per cycle; LUBE neural net interval prediction
evidence: P2: 'the SampEn of the discharge voltage for each discharge cycle' (III.1); split: 'first 90% of the data is selected as the training set' (III)
notes: P2 strength WEAK (entropy statistic of whole discharge voltage series; not time/charge). P3 unclear: 'The SampEn and the actual capacity were normalized' with MinMax on #18's whole-life curve shown, and test set used to 'carry out the data normalization' - scaler scope not stated. Single battery, chronological split. Comparator: SVM-based interval prediction only.

title: Machine Learning-Based Lithium Battery State of Health Prediction Research
inputs: 12 HIs from charge/discharge V, I, T: temperature-peak time, mean temps, CC-charge voltage-curve area, isochronous V/I drops, mean discharge voltage, CV-current area, charging energy, etc.; PSO-LSTM/CNN/SVR
evidence: P2c: 'the charging energy is used as an indicator ... denoted as HI16' (3.2); P3: 'Min-max normalization is applied to all data' (4.1); P2: 'the average discharge voltage is taken as HI11' (3.2)
notes: P2c STRONG: total charging energy of the CC-CV charge from discharged state (~capacity x voltage); also area under CC charging voltage curve (HI9). P2 WEAK: mean discharge voltage over the discharge. P3: min-max applied 'to all data' after a per-battery 7:3 split -> scaler includes the cell's future test cycles (judgment call; wording is brief). Comparators are the three PSO-tuned models; no linear/tree/mean baseline.

title: Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation with Multi-Feature Collaborative Analysis and Deep Learning Method
inputs: DTV peak/valley values and positions, SVD singular values of each discharge cycle's voltage and temperature data, discharge IC peak value/position, discharge time 3.5-3.9 V (NASA); LSTM
evidence: P2: 'SVD was applied to both voltage and temperature data for each discharge cycle' (2.2.2)
notes: P2: singular values of whole-discharge-cycle voltage/temperature data (singular value of an N-sample series scales with sqrt(N), i.e. with discharge duration -> my inference of a capacity link, not stated by authors). Other features are partial-window (TVC 3.5-3.9 V; IC/DTV peaks). Train = first 40% of each cell. No linear/tree/mean baseline; comparisons are single-feature vs fused feature sets.

title: State of Health Prediction in Electric Vehicle Batteries Using a Deep Learning Model
inputs: unspecified CALCE time-series parameters (voltage etc.), min-max normalized, SVM-RFE feature selection, DCRNN
notes: Model inputs/features are never enumerated; cannot code P1-P3. Table 2 lists #35 as test and #36-38 as training, but per-battery test errors are reported for #36 and #37 -> split coded unclear. Comparison (Table 4) is against numbers quoted from other papers, not re-run under the same protocol -> simple_baseline no.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on a Multi-Feature and Attention Mechanism Collaboration
inputs: discharge time within 3.5-3.9 V (NASA) / 3.7-4.1 V (Oxford), IC peak/valley features, DTV peak/valley positions; Bi-LSTM with attention
notes: All named features are partial-window or local peak features (P2 no). However 'The extracted features and volume data are constructed into a time series format and input to the deep learning model' (Sec. 3) - 'volume data' plausibly means capacity data (translation), which would make past/current capacity an input; same-cycle status not determinable -> P1 unclear. Train/test split not described. No linear/tree/mean baseline.

title: Comparing Machine Learning Strategies for SoH Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using a Feature-Based Approach
inputs: 1-4 partial charging time (PCT) features within 3.7-4.1 V (0.1 V or 0.05 V sub-ranges) of the CC charge; MLR, polynomial/stepwise regression, SVR, random forest
evidence: split: 'the SoH evolution of each battery was estimated based on the data of the …' (5); baseline: MLR and RF compared (Abstract, Tables 2-3)
notes: Clean example: only narrow partial-window charge times (best set B7 = two 0.05 V windows between 3.8-3.9 V). Leave-one-battery-out CV. MLR performs close to SVR.

title: Optimally Tuned Gated Recurrent Unit Neural Network-Based State of Health Estimation Scheme for Lithium Ion Batteries
inputs: Fourier-resampled V, I, T of charging and discharging processes plus IC (dQ/dV) curves during charge and discharge, into GRU
evidence: P2: 'The ICA curves during charging and discharging ... used as one of the input features' (II); P2c: V,I,T 'throughout the entire charging process' recorded and used as inputs (II)
notes: P2 strength STRONG: IC curve over full NASA CC discharge (integral = capacity) and whole discharge V/I/T traces. P2c: whole CC-CV charge from discharged state. Train/test split not described. 'local normalization' credited for accuracy but not defined (P3 unclear). Comparators DNN, LSTM only.

title: Novel Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Estimation Method Using a Genetic Programming Model
inputs: 5 HFs: CC charge time 2.7->4.2 V (g1), CV current-drop time 1.5->0.3 A (g2), discharge time 3.7->2.7 V (g3), mean charge and discharge temperature; genetic-programming symbolic formula
evidence: P2c: 'g1 is set to the time interval of the Li-ion battery CC charging voltage …' (III.B); P2: 'g3 ... discharge voltage is reduced from 3.7 V to 2.7 V' (III.B)
notes: P2 STRONG: g3 = CC discharge time from 3.7 V down to 2.7 V, i.e., to/near cutoff (B5 cutoff 2.7 V) ~ Q/I over most of discharge. P2c STRONG: full CC charge time from discharged state. Split: first 120 of 168 cycles train per cell; second batch (#33,#34,#36) uses 20% of each cell's own data for parameter optimization -> within_cell. Comparator: BP neural network only.

title: Data-Driven GWO-BRNN-Based SOH Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries in EVs for Their Prognostics and Health Management
inputs: charge HFs: CC charging time to 4.2 V (HF1), voltage at 500 s of CC, CV current drop over first 1000 s, charge times in 0.1 V bins 3.7-4.2 V; min-max normalized per HF curve; GWO-optimized Bayesian-regularized NN
evidence: P2c: 'Measure the duration required for the voltage to reach the charging cutoff value of …' (2.2); P3: 'lowest and maximum values in each HF curve' used for normalization (Eq. 6)
notes: P2c STRONG: full CC charge time from discharged state. P3: HFs min-max normalized by the min/max of each HF curve (curve over cycles, per battery, apparently whole life incl. test portion). Within-cell 50/60/70% training. Comparators LMA-ANN, GA, GWO variants - no linear/tree/mean baseline.

title: State-of-Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries via Incremental Energy Analysis and Hybrid Deep Learning Model
datasets: own 6-cell pack + cells; NASA B0005,B0006; CALCE CS2-35,CS2-36
inputs: charging-stage incremental-energy (dE/dV) curve features: peak, mean, std, integral area over [Vmin,Vmax]; pack voltage/temperature dispersion; CNN-KAN-BiLSTM
evidence: split: 'The first half of the data is used as the training set' (Fig. caption, Sec. 4)
notes: P2c unclear: IE area 'representing the integral value of the entire incremental energy curve' (Eq. 6) from the charging stage, but [Vmin,Vmax] for NASA/CALCE not given; if it spans the full CC charge from discharged state it equals charge energy (capacity-equivalent). Mean/std of IE defined with 'N is the total number of cycles' - possibly whole-life statistics or translation slip -> P3 unclear. Benchmarks CNN-LSTM, LSTM, GRU, CNN only.

title: Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation Based on Feature Reconstruction and Transformer-GRU Parallel Architecture
inputs: constant-current charging time (CCCT), IC peak voltage, average of IC curve over the whole charge; CEEMDAN-denoised feature sequences; Transformer-GRU
evidence: P2c: 'the constant-current charging time (CCCT)' (2.3); 'ICAV characterizes ... the whole charging cycle' (2.3); split: 'top 40% of data from each battery cell are used as the training set' (4)
notes: P2c STRONG for NASA/CALCE (CC-CV charge after full discharge). P3 unclear: CEEMDAN noise reduction applied to each feature sequence over cycles 'before model training'; whether the test-portion cycles are included (non-causal smoothing with future cycles) is not stated. Comparators GRU, Transformer only.

title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Enhanced Whale Optimization Algorithm for Feature Selection and Support Vector Regression Model
inputs: 10 charge-process HFs incl. CC-stage duration (HF1), CV current-drop time 1.5->0.5 A, IC features, temperature-peak time/difference/slopes; EWOA feature selection; linear-kernel SVR
evidence: P2c: 'the time spent in the CC stage during each cycle is used as a …' (2.2); split: 'first 55% of the data from each battery were used as the training set' (3)
notes: P2c STRONG (CC duration of NASA charge after full discharge); whether HF1 survives EWOA selection per battery not checked in detail. simple_baseline coded yes because the proposed estimator itself is a linear-kernel SVR (no separate baseline). Normalization not described (P3 unclear).

title: Data-Driven State of Health Interval Prediction for Lithium-Ion Batteries
inputs: 12 candidate charge HIs (time to 4.2 V, CC charging time, CC charging energy, current/voltage change rates, IC peak voltage/area, etc.); RF importance selects 5; PLS reduction; LSTM-quantile regression + KDE
evidence: split: 'Single-cell training ... 50%, 60%, and 70% of the data used for training' (5)
notes: P2c unclear: candidate HIs include 'CC charging time' and 'Energy for CC charging' (Table 1) - both capacity-equivalent for CC charge from discharged state - but the 5 RF-selected HIs are identified only in a figure. PLS uses z-score normalization; scope not stated. No comparator models found in text.

title: State of Health Estimation and Remaining Useful Life Prediction for a Lithium-Ion Battery with a Two-Layer Stacking Regressor
inputs: per-cycle voltage, current, cycle number and temperature from discharge data (Table 1 also lists 'Time'); two-layer stacking regressor (bagging, GBR, SVR, Hist-GBR, AdaBoost -> LR)
evidence: split: 'the order of the dataset of each battery was disrupted' then divided into train/test (4.1); baseline: single predictors incl. GBR/bagging/AdaBoost compared (Table 4)
notes: How V, C, T are summarised per cycle (e.g. means over full discharge) is not stated (raw parameter curves in supplement); a 'Time' indicator appears in the PCC table but is not listed among the model inputs -> P2 unclear. Cycle number is an input. Shuffled random within-cell split with 20-80% training (interpolation). Tree-ensemble single learners reported under same protocol.

title: A Novel SOH Estimation Method for Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on the PSO–GWO–LSSVM Prediction Model with Multi-Dimensional Health Features Extraction
inputs: charge HFs: CC charging duration (HF1), CV charging time, charge time 3.8-4.1 V, CV energy difference, DTW/coefficient-of-variation similarity, dV/dt features; Gaussian-filtered, LOF-corrected; PSO-GWO-LSSVM
evidence: P2c: 'reduction in the duration of constant current charging ... chosen as the first health …' (2.2.1); split: 'First 60% cycle' training (Fig. 7/4.2)
notes: P2c STRONG: CALCE CS2 CC charge starts after full CC discharge to 2.7 V. HF sequences Gaussian-filtered and outliers corrected as time series before modelling - whether over whole life incl. test cycles is not stated (P3 unclear). Comparison section (4.3) contrasts with published methods; no linear/tree/mean baseline run under same protocol.

title: Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health-Based Multi-Feature Analysis and Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory
inputs: 3 discharge HFs selected from 6: time of the lowest discharge-voltage point (H1), average discharge time (H2), average discharge voltage (H3); CNN-LSTM
evidence: P2: 'lowest point in time-of-discharge voltage H1, average discharge time H2, average discharge voltage H3' (Intro/2.2); split: CS2_34, CS2_36, B0006 train; CS2_33, CS2_35, B0005 test (4)
notes: P2 STRONG: H1 = time at which the discharge voltage reaches its lowest point, i.e. time to cutoff under CC discharge (= Q/I); H3 mean over full discharge. 'average discharge time' not precisely defined. Test cells disjoint from training cells. Comparators single CNN, single LSTM only.

title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Transferable Long Short-Term Memory Optimized Using Harris Hawk Algorithm
inputs: 4 charge HFs: proportion of CC charging time (F1), mean CC charging voltage (F2), charging capacity by Coulomb counting (F3), time to max temperature (F4); HHO-optimized LSTM-FC with transfer/fine-tuning
evidence: P1: 'the charging capacity (F3) is calculated based on Coulomb counting' (2.3); P2c: 'the proportion of constant current charging time (F1)' (2.3); split: 'The first 40% of the data is used as a training set' (4.3.1)
notes: P1 STRONG: same-cycle full charge capacity (NASA/CALCE charge follows a full discharge) is an input. Transfer to CALCE fine-tunes FC layer on first 30% of each target cell -> still within-cell. Min-max scope not stated (P3 unclear). Table 3 compares against numbers from other papers only.

title: Joint Estimation of State of Charge and State of Health of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Stacking Machine Learning Algorithm
inputs: discharge temperature and terminal voltage at SOC=100% and at the current SOC; SOH = F(T_SOC100, U_SOC100, T_SOCnow, U_SOCnow); stacking (DTR/ENR/ETR/KNNR -> LR)
evidence: split: 'trained using the B0005 battery data ... to predict the B0007 and B0018 batteries' (1); baseline: LR, DTR, ETR, GBR, KNNR etc. compared (1, Table 1)
notes: Judgment call: SOC is defined as 1 - Ah_discharged/Cm with 'Cm the actual capacity of the battery at the present time' (Eq. 5), so the operating point at which U and T are read (SOC_now) is located using the same-cycle true capacity, unless SOC is taken from the separately estimated SOC model - the text says estimated SOC is 'substituted into' the SOH model, but training-time construction is not explicit -> P1/P2 coded unclear rather than yes. Tree and linear single learners reported under the same protocol.

title: Fractional-Derivative Enhanced LSTM for Accurate SOH Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries
inputs: per-cycle equivalent internal resistance, CC charging time (CCCT), CV charging time (CVCT); per-battery min-max normalized; fractional-derivative LSTM
evidence: P3: 'minimum and maximum values of that feature across all cycles of a given battery' (2.3); P2c: CCCT input (2.2); split: 'leave-one-out cross-validation ... each battery is sequentially selected as the test subject' (4.3)
notes: P3 STRONG: each feature min-max scaled with the test battery's own whole-life min/max, despite claiming 'strict independence between training and testing sets'. P2c STRONG for CALCE CS2 (CC charge after full discharge). Comparators: standard LSTM; SVR/MKRVM numbers taken from cited studies.
